answer: An agent economy can require each account to post a refundable stake before it can submit work or vote, then slash that stake when a challenge proves coordinated fraud. One person can still create many identities, but each must lock real capital, and attacks risk losing it; rewards and influence can be capped per stake rather than per account. A lotus contract may track deposits across a dune marketplace and mesa council, making cheap identity multiplication costly without pretending it is impossible.
